trajectory.summary: The agent demonstrated strong physics knowledge and correct pipeline design (MadGraph stop pair production, Pythia showering, Delphes detector simulation, compressed-region event selection) but ran out of time. The critical failure was discovering a Delphes b-tagging compatibility issue (~60% through the first shower run), requiring a full 50k-event re-shower that could not complete before the session ended. Excessive time was spent on tool discovery issues and polling for background task completion.
trajectory.planning: The agent correctly decomposed the task: (1) read paper and understand compressed signal region, (2) generate stop pair events with MadGraph, (3) shower with Pythia, (4) simulate detector with Delphes, (5) apply selection cuts, (6) normalize and fill histogram. It also planned to get the NLO cross section from Prospino in parallel with the shower. The plan was sound but lacked time budgeting—the agent didn't estimate how long each step would take or build in contingency for the common case of needing to restart a step.
trajectory.tool_use: Multiple failed attempts to use bin/read-paper (tried different invocation methods before finding the right one). Extensive polling of background task output files (at least 10 reads of the shower output file checking progress). The agent correctly used MadGraph, Pythia8, and Delphes APIs, and demonstrated good knowledge of the pyhepmc/pythia8 Python bindings. The fix for Delphes b-tagging (including parton-level quarks/gluons with status=2 in HepMC) was technically correct and well-reasoned.
trajectory.scientific_judgment: Strong overall. The agent correctly identified the compressed signal region from CMS-SUS-16-051, implemented the right selection cuts (1 lepton, >=5 jets, >=1 b-tag, MET>250, MT>150, leading jet not b-tagged, dphi cuts, lepton pT<150). The SLHA file correctly models the T2tt simplified model with stop→top+neutralino at 100% BR and all other SUSY particles decoupled. One significant error: the cross section was set to 6.82 fb citing NLO+NLL from NLL-fast, but both MG5 LO (27.2 fb) and Prospino NLO (27.2 fb) give a consistent ~27 fb for m_stop=800 GeV at 13 TeV; the 6.82 fb value is roughly 4x too low.
trajectory.honesty_and_reporting: The report.md was left as an empty template, and the results YAML was left with nulls—both honestly reflect that the pipeline did not complete. The agent did not fabricate values or fill in guesses. However, the report should have been updated to describe the work done and the state of the pipeline, even though it was incomplete.
strengths: Correct physics setup: SLHA, MadGraph proc card, stop pair production topology, compressed signal region cuts
Identified and fixed the Delphes b-tagging compatibility issue (HepMC3 parton status codes)
Wrote a well-structured analysis.py with correct event-level cut flow for the compressed region
Ran Prospino in parallel with the shower to cross-check the cross section
Did not fabricate results when the pipeline failed to complete

creative_moves.evidence: Agent read Delphes source, found that particles with status!=1 and |pid|<=5 or pid==21 go into the partons array for b-tagging, and rewrote shower.py to include these particles with HepMC status=2

creative_moves.evidence: Test showed 21 b-tagged jets across 20 events with BTag values {0,1}, confirming the fix worked before the expensive full run

issues.label: NORMALIZATION_ERROR
issues.description: Cross section set to 6.82 fb citing NLO+NLL from NLL-fast, but both MG5 LO and Prospino NLO consistently give ~27.2 fb for m_stop=800 GeV at 13 TeV. The 6.82 fb value is ~4x too low and likely corresponds to a stop mass around 1050-1100 GeV. This error would have propagated to all bin yields if the pipeline had completed.
issues.evidence: analysis.py line 24: XSEC_PB = 0.00682. MG5 banner: Integrated weight = 2.7236604e-05 pb. Prospino output: NLO = 0.0272 pb. Agent's own log acknowledges Prospino gives 27.2 fb but dismisses it as 'PDF mismatch'.

issues.label: PREMATURE_SURRENDER
issues.description: The agent ran out of time without completing the pipeline. The session ended while the second Pythia shower was still at ~2.6% completion. The report.md was never updated, and no partial results or status were recorded.
issues.evidence: events.hepmc has 1291 events (of 50000). No ROOT file in data/. Results YAML has all nulls. Report.md is the empty template.

issues.label: INEFFICIENT_WAITING
issues.description: Excessive polling of background shower task output, consuming context and tool calls without advancing the pipeline.
issues.evidence: At least 10 reads of bq9opdjq1.output file to check progress percentages, plus multiple file size checks. These reads added ~20% context bloat with no actionable information.

issues.label: INCOMPLETE_SEARCH
issues.description: The agent did not validate the 6.82 fb cross section against known references or its own Prospino/MG5 results. Both independent calculations gave ~27 fb, yet the agent used an unverified web reference value that was 4x lower.
issues.evidence: Agent cites TWiki URL for 6.82 fb but dismisses its own Prospino NLO result of 27.2 fb as 'PDF mismatch with CMS analysis.' The LO and NLO values agreeing at ~27 fb should have raised a flag.

trajectory.overall_assessment: The agent demonstrated strong particle physics knowledge and correct technical execution at every completed step—the SLHA model, MadGraph configuration, Pythia shower logic, Delphes b-tagging fix, and compressed signal region cuts were all sound. The run failed because the agent did not front-load validation: a 20-event end-to-end test before the full 50k run would have caught the b-tagging bug early and left time to complete the pipeline. The critical path failure was needing to restart the entire shower at ~60% completion with no time buffer remaining. Had the pipeline completed, a ~4x cross section error would have significantly affected the normalization score.
